zh: 对位置 i，包含 i 且 i 是最大值（允许并列）的最长区间，左右边界恰好是两侧最近的“严格更高”的人；只有严格更高者才会挡住，等高的人可以包含进来。
设 L 为左侧最近严格更高的位置（没有则为 −1），R 为右侧最近严格更高的位置（没有则为 n），i 的区间长度就是 R−L−1。用单调栈两次扫描求出所有 L 和 R。
从左到右扫描：弹出所有身高 ≤ 当前值的栈顶位置，剩下的栈顶就是 L，然后压入 i；从右到左同样处理得到 R。注意两侧都用 ≤ 弹栈，否则 [2,2] 会算错。最后对 R−L−1 求和，最大约 10¹⁰，要用 64 位整数。
en: For position i, the longest range containing i in which i is a maximum (ties allowed) is bounded on each side exactly by the nearest strictly taller person; only strictly taller people block, and equally tall people can be included.
Let L be the nearest strictly taller position on the left (-1 if none) and R the nearest on the right (n if none); i's region length is R - L - 1. Two monotonic-stack scans give all L and R.

Scan left to right: pop every stack position whose height is <= the current value; the remaining top is L, then push i. Do the same from right to left to get R. Pop with <= on both sides, otherwise [2, 2] comes out wrong. Sum R - L - 1; it can reach about 10^10, so use a 64-bit integer.

explanationEn:
## Fixed original source and corrections to the description

The file fastprep/The D. E. Shaw Group/deshaw-calculate-total-region.md at fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc specifies: each student's region is the length of the longest contiguous subarray that contains their index and in which their height equals the maximum of the subarray. Return the sum of all region lengths. "Equals the maximum" here allows several people to tie for tallest; being the unique tallest is not required. The statement itself specifies 1 <= n <= 100000 and 1 <= heights[i] <= 10^9 and returns a long; ranges are not borrowed from other problems of the same company.

The official Output of the first original example [3,5,6] is 6, and the per-person lengths 1, 2, 3 also sum to 6. However, the end of the explanation adds a note that "the answer in the source image is 5, which is confusing"; the fixed snapshot has no readable original image supporting it. This site discloses that conflicting note but adopts the official output 6, which follows the explicit definition and can be recomputed, instead of treating the hearsay note as another rule. The official output 5 of the second original example [1,2,1] is correct: the middle student's longest range is the whole [1,2,1], of length 3; the original explanation wrongly wrote [1,2], and this site explicitly corrects that omission.

The two original examples keep 6 and 5; the third public example [2,2] is this site's addition, where everyone can take the whole array, so the answer is 4. The compiled code pops the stack with <= on one side and < on the other, which treats equally tall people on one side as obstacles and wrongly gives 3 on [2,2]. In this problem only strictly taller people block, on both sides. The input protocol is n followed by n heights, and the output is one exact integer. Upstream code was not executed.

## Approach

For each index i, find the nearest position L on the left that is strictly taller than heights[i] and the nearest strictly taller position R on the right; use -1 and n respectively when none exists. The region length is R - L - 1. Use two monotonic-stack scans: when a new height arrives, pop every old position whose height is less than or equal to it, and the remaining top of the stack is the nearest strictly taller one. Use <= on both sides; duplicate values must not be assigned different ownership.

## Proof of correctness

A valid range containing i cannot extend past L or R, otherwise it would contain a strictly taller person and heights[i] would no longer equal the maximum. There is no strictly taller person between L and R, so the whole open interval (L, R) is itself valid and contains i. Hence it is exactly the longest range, with length R - L - 1.

During the left-to-right scan, the positions in the stack increase and their heights strictly decrease. An old position popped by a new one is not taller than the new value: for any future position, if the old position would be strictly taller, the new position is too and is closer; if the new position is not tall enough, the old positions it popped are not tall enough either. So popping never loses a future nearest strictly taller answer. After popping, the stack top is exactly the nearest strictly taller person on the left of the current position; the right-hand scan is symmetric. Computing every length correctly and summing gives the required total.

## Complexity and numeric bounds

Each index is pushed and popped at most once per scan: O(n) time and O(n) space. Each region is at most n, so the sum is at most n^2, reached when everyone is equally tall. For n = 100000 the answer 10000000000 exceeds 32 bits but is far below the signed 64-bit limit, so 64-bit or arbitrary-precision integers are required. For strictly increasing or decreasing arrays it is n(n+1)/2.

## Independent verification

A small oracle extends the right end for each left end in turn, maintains the range maximum, records for every index equal to that maximum the longest length achievable, and finally sums per person; it does not look for nearest taller boundaries. 163 unique inputs went through a real reference subprocess, and all 3279 arrays with n = 1..7 and values 1/2/3 were checked exhaustively.

The full n = 100000 stress test uses a different algorithm: sort by height, activate positions from low to high, and merge adjacent activated cells with union-find; for one height, activate and merge all of its positions first, then read the component sizes of those positions. At that point the activated cells are exactly the positions with height <= the current value, and the component is the longest selectable range. Equal heights must be processed as a batch; you cannot read an answer right after activating one of them. This oracle is an O(n log n) sort plus near-linear union-find and does not call the reference monotonic stack.

The official data cover all-equal arrays, increasing and decreasing arrays, 1 and 10^9 alternating, long plateaus, tallest at both ends, a unique tallest in the middle, repeated maxima, zigzags and fixed-seed random arrays. All-equal and monotone cases are additionally checked against closed forms, and every large case was executed through the reference subprocess. The negative controls are asymmetric handling of equal heights and 32-bit sum overflow; a kill only counts after every official case exits normally.
